c74object.name: mUnit.teardown
c74object.digest: Bang once the results are final, so a test patch can clean up
c74object.description: mUnit.teardown is the counterpart of mUnit.loadbang: it bangs once mUnit.handler has frozen the results of the patch it is in, so the patch can clean up (stop a metro or DSP, close a file, reset a global). The results are already final, so a teardown can't change a verdict, and the handler waits for every teardown to report done before it closes patches or quits Max.
c74object.discussion: In the usual case, every patch open at once, it fires after the result files are written, before mUnit.harness closes the patches or the command-line runner quits Max. With mUnit.harness in sequential mode it fires after the patch's asserts have settled and before that patch is closed, while the suite goes on. The handler waits up to teardownMs (default 2000 ms), and warns in the console about any teardown that didn't report. By default an object reports done as soon as its outlet has fired; with hold it waits for a message on its inlet instead. Console errors while teardowns run are kept in the log but never fail the suite. Don't drive asserts from a teardown.

inlet.digest: With @hold 1: any message reports the cleanup done

outlet.digest: Bang once the results of this patch are final

method.name: anything
method.description: With hold 1, any message (done by convention) tells the handler this teardown has finished. Without hold, the inlet does nothing.

attribute.name: hold
attribute.digest: Wait for a message on the inlet before reporting done (default 0)
attribute.description: For cleanup that takes time. The handler waits up to teardownMs; if the message never comes it goes on anyway and warns.

entry.name: bang
entry.description: Out the outlet: a bang once the results of this patch are final, so the patch can clean up (stop DSP, close files, reset a global).
